title: HA Button Restore
summary: Give a temporary button action an intelligent restore. Capture selected HA entity states before a sequence such as lights off and dehumidifiers off; later restore only devices that have not received a newer HA control command. The logic runs inside Home Assistant, without a browser or Projects server staying open.
features: Remember selected entity states under a named key before changing them.
Restore eligible captured entities once using the same key.
A newer HA service command invalidates restoration for that device, even if its displayed state did not change.
Related control entities on the same registered device invalidate together.
Discard a remembered group without restoring it.
Works with any button integration that exposes usable triggers; this component does not discover press types.
workflows: Suppose a lamp is on. A single press captures that state, then switches the lamp off for a temporary scene.
A double press restores the lamp only if no newer HA command has claimed it. If a scheduled lights-off automation ran in the meantime, the lamp stays off.
Use the same key for capture and restore. Separate unrelated buttons/scenes with different keys to avoid replacing each other’s snapshots.
Assign a group to one button
Identify the exact single-press trigger provided by your physical button integration. Choose the devices to affect.
In the single-press automation, call mungoon_button_restore.capture first, with key and entity_id list. Follow it with the desired light, fan, switch or other HA actions.
In the double-press automation, call mungoon_button_restore.restore with that same key. There is no need to manually guess the previous on/off values.
Start with one test light, then expand the group. Confirm your button supports double press; a label in a builder cannot create an event the hardware never emits.
Test a later automation taking priority
Turn the test light on, trigger capture followed by off, then issue a separate lights-off command from HA.
Trigger restore. The test light should remain off because the later command takes priority, even though it was already visibly off.
Repeat without the intervening command. Restore should now return the remembered state.
For a multi-entity device, test the actual control entity your other automations use. Device-registry grouping is important to the priority behaviour.
Discard or replace a saved scene
Call mungoon_button_restore.clear with the key when the temporary scene should be forgotten.
Capturing under an existing key replaces its old snapshot. Restore consumes the snapshot, so pressing restore twice does not repeat an old scene.
After HA restart, integration unload or scene reload, take a new capture. Snapshots are held in memory, not a persistent undo history.
limits: Direct changes through a physical remote or vendor application may not produce a HA service event and are not universally tracked. This is targeted restore, not general undo. Eight policy tests passed previously; a clean HA installation has not been rerun for this documentation update.
